`scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs` still computes the count at the divergence listing and prints it one line below. Unchanged.

## ⭐ Triage's third-carrier candidate — READ, and the answer is NO

The grading comment names `scripts/shadcn-sync.js:469` as a **candidate** and is explicit that it did not read the context, so it is ⛔ not an assertion. This seat read it. **It is not a third carrier**, and the reason is the decision rule triage itself wrote.

Measured tree-wide, `localLines` and `shadcnLines` have exactly **four** occurrences — and all four are inside `shadcn-sync.js`:

| site | what it is |
|:--|:--|
| `:469` | `const localLines = localContent.split('\n').length` |
| `:505` | `const shadcnLines = shadcnContent.split('\n').length` |
| `:546`, `:547` | the two names placed on the returned result object |

⛔ **There is no consumer.** Nothing reads `.localLines` or `.shadcnLines` — not in `scripts/`, not in `scripts/__tests__`, not anywhere in the tree. And the three messages in that file that do print a line count —

```
`${localOnly.length} local line(s) upstream lacks — --update would refuse`
`${upstreamOnly.length} upstream line(s) to pick up — safe to sync`
`✗ Refusing to overwrite ${name}.tsx — ${lost.length} local line(s) upstream does not have:`
```

— all read the **array lengths returned by `localOnlyLines()`**, ⛔ not the split counts. ⇒ by triage's own test (「把整段文本的长度当作『有几行』打印出来」), this number is never printed as a line count and never compared, so the off-by-one has nowhere to surface.

**Radius, so the zero is a reading**: two scans at two different refs, both with a control that fired. ① the GitHub API over all **295** files in `scripts/` + `scripts/__tests__` at `main` = `272a53066`; ② a read-only grep of the whole checkout (all `.js`/`.mjs`/`.ts`/`.tsx`, `node_modules` excluded) at its HEAD `3ecc369bf`. Both returned the same four hits. ⚠️ **Outside that radius**: any consumer reaching those properties dynamically (a computed key, a spread into something serialised) would be invisible to a name-based grep.

⇒ ⛔ **Do not fold `shadcn-sync.js` into this round.** It is out of the card's population. ⚠️ Whether two computed-and-never-read properties are worth a finding of their own is a different question and ⛔ not this card's; report it rather than acting on it.

## What the delivery owes — triage's words, binding

> ⭐ 修法⛔ 不是「减一了事」:要**同笔**加一条会因旧行为变红的断言(一个以换行结尾的片段,其打印计数必须等于 `wc -l`),否则下一次重写会把它带回来。

So: an assertion that **fails on the pre-repair code**, seen red first. ⚠️ And note the sibling round's constraint, which this seat is carrying forward rather than making the dev rediscover: the repair is a **trailing-terminator drop**, ⛔ not a blanket `length - 1` — a snippet that does **not** end in a newline must keep its true last line. ⭐ objectui#9921 landed a named `fileLines` helper in `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` that states the reasoning in full; read it before choosing a shape. ⚠️ It is a **different** population and a different instrument, so ⛔ reusing it is a judgement to make and defend, ⛔ not an instruction from this seat.

## Landed — PR objectui#9957, merged `2026-09-18T21:20:29Z`, squash `beb7ea4ce`

Card released: `pm:dispatched` removed, assignee cleared, read back **`MATCHES`**. ⛔ No patch round. **62b FIRED** (`M^ = aced50d2e`, `compare M^…head` = **diverged**, ahead 1 / behind 1).

### Landing probe on `main` = `beb7ea4ce` — ten tokens, all OK

| token | expectation |
|:--|:--|
| the named `snippetLineCount` helper | present |
| the single trailing-terminator pop | present |
| the raw `d.ported.split('\n').length` at the listing site | **absent** |
| the listing calling the helper | present |
| any blanket `.split('\n').length - 1` | **absent** |
| **any count written into the docblock** (`113`, `38`) | **absent** — commandment #9 |
| the UNTERMINATED fixture case | present |
| the wiring test's relational case | present |
| `fileLines` imported into this gate | **absent** — the judgement held |
| `shadcn-sync.js` untouched | **absent of any edit** — the turn-back held |

### ⭐ What this round actually settled

**Triage left a candidate unread, on purpose, and said so.** Its grading swept for a third carrier — 20 files matching `split('\n').length`, control 109 matching any `split('\n')` so the reader demonstrably responds — classified them by use, and named `scripts/shadcn-sync.js` as a candidate it had ⛔ not read. That is the good shape: a candidate published *as* a candidate.

**The answer is NO, and it took two readers to close it properly.** This seat measured that `localLines` / `shadcnLines` have four occurrences tree-wide, all inside that one file, with no consumer — at two refs, each with a control. ⚠️ But a name-based grep cannot see a computed key or a spread, and this seat said so rather than claiming a clean zero. The `os-dev` seat then closed exactly that gap: the result object is consumed only by named property access, there is no spread of a result, no `JSON.stringify` of one, and the file's only `Object.values` iterates the result **buckets** rather than a result's keys. ⇒ ⛔ not a third carrier, by a route the first reading could not reach.

⭐⭐ **The repair's own reasoning is the keeper.** The dev declined to import `fileLines` from `cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` — same repair, different population — and the load-bearing half of its reason was measured, not asserted: that census is **report-only by design** (its `ENFORCEMENT` constant reads `report-only`), while this gate runs **bare in `lint.yml`**, so a non-zero exit fails the job. ⇒ importing would hand a blocking gate a failure surface it is not responsible for. ⛔ Cross-script import was never the objection; coupling a blocking gate to a report-only module was.

⭐⭐⭐ **And the fixture reasoning is the sharpest thing in the round**: the pinned population is 113 of 113 newline-terminated, so **no tree-derived assertion can see the case a blanket subtraction would break**. That case is carried as a fixture precisely because the tree cannot supply it. ⇒ **the shape a later rewrite gets wrong is often the shape the tree has no instance of.**

### ⚠️ CI, and a refinement to the standing shard item

All 35 green on this head, ⛔ no re-run needed. Shard margins: 1/4 **912s** (+288s), 2/4 800s (+400s), 4/4 1053s (+147s), **3/4 1073s (+127s)**.
⇒ ⭐ the slowest shard on this head was **3/4**, not 1/4. Taken with the previous round — where 1/4 ran 1216s then 1167s on the same commit — **the ceiling risk is ⛔ not confined to one shard**, and a repair that only rebalanced the shard that happened to fail would not address it. 🧑 This sharpens objectui#9584 rather than changing it.

### ⛔ Turned back, ⛔ not widened into

`scripts/shadcn-sync.js` computes `localLines` and `shadcnLines` and puts both on a returned object that nothing ever reads. Reported, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not tidied — the values are never read, so the off-by-one inside them cannot surface; it is not a reproducible defect, not a declared-contract violation, and not a metadata trap. Named here so the next person to touch that file has the reading.

⛔ **No dwell figure is published**, for the third round running — the `added_to_merge_queue` event is unreadable here, so the clock that would anchor one cannot be read (item ⑫).
